questions.q: The 'Common Carbon Metric', supported by UNEP, has been developed for
options: assessing the carbon footprint of building operations around the world
enabling commercial farming entities around the world to enter carbon emission trading
enabling governments to assess the overall carbon footprint caused by their countries
assessing the overall carbon footprint caused by the use of fossil fuels by the world in a unit time
questions.explain: The Common Carbon Metric is supported by the United Nations Environment Program. Its purpose is to give the building sector a way to measure, report, and verify greenhouse gas emission reductions consistently and comparably. It is used to measure, report, and verify GHG emissions related to the operation of different types of buildings in different climate zones.

questions.q:
With reference to the 'New York Declaration on Forests', which of the following statements are correct?
1. It was first endorsed at the United Nations Climate Summit in 2014.
2. It endorses a global timeline to end the loss of forests.
3. It is a legally binding international declaration.
4. It is endorsed by governments, big companies and indigenous communities.
5. India was one of the signatories at its inception.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explain:
Statements 1 and 2 are correct: The New York Declaration on Forests was adopted in 2014 at the UN Secretary-General's Climate Summit. It calls for ending natural forest loss and restoring degraded landscapes.

Statement 3 is not correct: It is not a legally binding declaration but entirely voluntary.

Statement 4 is correct: It was endorsed by nearly 200 governments, companies, Indigenous Peoples, and civil society organizations.

Statement 5 is not correct: India is not a signatory to the treaty.

questions.q: 'R2 Code of Practices' constitutes a tool available for promoting the adoption of
options: environmentally responsible practices in electronics recycling industry
ecological management of 'Wetlands of International Importance' under the Ramsar Convention
sustainable practices in the cultivation of agricultural crops in degraded lands
'Environmental Impact Assessment' in the exploitation of natural resources
questions.explain: Responsible Recycling (R2) is a standard specifically created for the electronics recycling industry by Sustainable Electronics Recycling International (SERI). The R2 Code of Practices promotes environmentally responsible practices in electronics recycling.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement 1: The United Nations Capital Development Fund (UNCDF) and the Arbor Day Foundation have recently recognized Hyderabad as 2020 Tree City of the World.
Statement 2: Hyderabad was selected for the recognition for a year following its commitment to grow and maintain the urban forests.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: Both Statement 1 and Statement 2 are correct and Statement 2 is the correct explanation for Statement 1
Both Statement 1 and Statement 2 are correct but Statement 2 is not the correct explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is correct but Statement 2 is not correct
Statement 1 is not correct but Statement 2 is correct
questions.explain: Hyderabad has become the only city in India to be recognised as a 'Tree City of the World' by the Arbor Day Foundation and the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) of the United Nations. Hyderabad was recognized for its commitment to growing and maintaining urban forests.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Ramsar Convention, it is mandatory on the part of the Government of India to protect and conserve all the wetlands in the territory of India.
2. The Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2010 were framed by the Government of India based on the recommendation of the Ramsar Convention.
3. The Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2010 also encompass the drainage area or catchment regions of the wetlands as determined by the authority.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain:
Statement 1 is not correct: The Ramsar Convention guides parties to protect wetlands but does not mandate it.

Statement 2 is not correct: The Wetlands Rules 2010 were not based on Ramsar Convention recommendations.

Statement 3 is correct: The Wetlands Rules 2010 include drainage areas and catchment regions of wetlands as determined by the authority.

questions.q: The Partnership for Action on Green Economy (PAGE), a UN mechanism to assist countries transition towards greener and more inclusive economies, emerged at
options: The Earth Summit on Sustainable Development 2002, Johannesburg
The United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development 2012, Rio de Janeiro
The United Nations Framework Convention on Climate change 2015, Paris
The World Sustainable Development Summit 2016, New Delhi
questions.explain: The Partnership for Action on Green Economy (PAGE) emerged at The United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development 2012 in Rio de Janeiro. PAGE seeks to put sustainability at the heart of economic policies to advance the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.

questions.q: Momentum for Change: Climate Neutral Now is an initiative launched by
options: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change
questions.explain: Momentum for Change: Climate Neutral Now is an initiative launched by the UNFCCC Secretariat in 2015. It aims to encourage individuals, companies and governments to measure their climate footprint, reduce emissions, and offset what they cannot reduce with UN-certified emission reductions.

questions.q:
With reference to the 'Global Alliance for Climate-Smart Agriculture (GACSA)', which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. GACSA is an outcome of the Climate Summit held in Paris in 2015.
2. Membership of GACSA does not create any binding obligations.
3. India was instrumental in the creation of GACSA.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explain:
Statement 1 is not correct: GACSA was launched in September 2014 on the margins of the UN Climate Summit, not in Paris in 2015.

Statement 2 is correct: Membership in GACSA does not create any binding obligations. Members determine their particular voluntary actions.

Statement 3 is not correct: India was not instrumental in the creation of GACSA, though some Indian NGOs are members.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Climate and Clean Air Coalition (CCAC) to Reduce Short Lived Climate Pollutants is a unique initiative of G2O group of countries.
2. The CCAC focuses on methane, black carbon, and hydrofluorocarbons.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is not correct: The Climate and Clean Air Coalition (CCAC) is a voluntary partnership of governments, intergovernmental organizations, businesses, scientific institutions, and civil society organizations. It is not an initiative of the G20 group of countries.\n\nStatement 2 is correct: The CCAC focuses on methane, black carbon, and hydrofluorocarbons, which are the most important contributors to the artificial global greenhouse effect after carbon dioxide.

questions.q: With reference to Trade Related Analysis of Fauna and Flora in Commerce (TRAFFIC), which of the following statements is/are correct?\n1. TRAFFIC is a bureau under the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP).\n2. The mission of TRAFFIC is to ensure that trade in wild plants and animals is not a threat to the conservation of nature.
questions.explain: Statement 1 is incorrect: TRAFFIC is a leading non-governmental organisation working globally on trade in wild animals and plants in the context of both biodiversity conservation and sustainable development. It is not a bureau under UNEP.\n\nStatement 2 is correct: The mission of TRAFFIC is to ensure that trade in wild plants and animals is not a threat to the conservation of nature.

questions.q:
The FAO accords the status of the Globally Important Agricultural Heritage System (GIAHS) to traditional agricultural systems. What is the overall goal of this initiative?
1. To provide modern technology, training in modern farming methods and financial support to local communities of identified GIAHS so as to greatly enhance their agricultural productivity.
2. To identify and safeguard eco-friendly traditional farm practices and their associated landscapes, agricultural biodiversity, and knowledge systems of the local communities.
3. To provide Geographical Indication status to all the varieties of agricultural produce in such identifies GIAHS.
questions.explain:
Statement 1 is incorrect: GIAHS aims to identify, support and safeguard globally important agricultural heritage systems and their livelihoods, agricultural and associated biodiversity, knowledge systems, cultures and landscapes around the world. It focuses on traditional methods, not modern ones.

Statement 2 is correct: GIAHS will identify and safeguard eco-friendly traditional farm practices and their associated landscapes, agricultural biodiversity and knowledge systems of the local communities.

Statement 3 is incorrect: Geographical Indication status is not associated with GIAHS.

questions.q:
With reference to an initiative called 'The Economics of Ecosystems and Biodiversity (TEEB)', which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. It is an initiative hosted by UNEP, IMF and World Economic Forum.
2. It is a global initiative that focuses on drawing attention to the economic benefits of biodiversity.
3. It presents an approach that can help decision makers recognize, demonstrate, and capture the value of ecosystems and biodiversity.
questions.explain:
Statement 1 is incorrect: TEEB is not hosted by UNEP, IMF and World Economic Forum. It was launched at the G8 meeting of environment ministers in 2007 and is managed by UNEP as part of its Green Economy Initiative.

Statement 2 is correct: TEEB is a global initiative focused on drawing attention to the economic benefits of biodiversity.

Statement 3 is correct: TEEB presents an approach that can help decision-makers recognize, demonstrate and capture the value of ecosystems and biodiversity.

questions.q:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?
Proper design and effective implementation of UNREDD+ Programme can significantly contribute to
1. Protection of biodiversity
2. Resilience of forest ecosystems
3. Poverty reduction
questions.explain: All statements are correct. The REDD+ program aims to reduce deforestation and forest degradation, improve livelihoods, reduce poverty, and mitigate climate change. It incorporates benefits of biodiversity conservation, improves resilience of forest ecosystems, and contributes to poverty reduction.

questions.q:
What is/are the importance/importances of the 'United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification'?
1. It aims to promote effective action through innovative national programmes and supportive international partnerships.
2. It has a special/particular focus on South Asia and North Africa regions, and its Secretariat facilitates the allocation of major portions of financial resources to these regions.
3. It is committed to a bottom-up approach, encouraging the participation of local people in combating desertification.
questions.explain:
Statement 1 is correct: UNCCD aims to promote effective action through innovative national programmes and supportive international partnerships.

Statement 2 is incorrect: UNCCD does not have a special focus on South Asia and North Africa regions.

Statement 3 is correct: UNCCD is committed to a bottom-up approach, encouraging the participation of local people in combating desertification.

questions.q:
With reference to an organisation known as 'BirdLife International', which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. It is a Global Partnership of Conservation Organisations.
2. The concept of 'biodiversity hotspots' originated from this organisation.
3. It identifies the sites known/referred to as 'Important Bird and Biodiversity Areas'.
questions.explain:
Statement 1 is correct: BirdLife International is a global partnership of conservation organisations.

Statement 2 is incorrect: The concept of 'biodiversity hotspots' originated from Conservation International, not BirdLife International.

Statement 3 is correct: BirdLife International identifies sites known as 'Important Bird and Biodiversity Areas'.

questions.q: Which one of the following is associated with the issue of control and phasing out of the use of ozone-depleting substances?
questions.explain: The Montreal Protocol is an international treaty designed to protect the ozone layer by phasing out the production of numerous substances that are responsible for ozone depletion. It was agreed on 16 September 1987 and entered into force on 1 January 1989.

questions.q:
With reference to the International Union for Conservation of Nature and Natural Resource (IUCN) and the Convention of International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES), which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. IUCN is an organ of the United Nations and CITES is an international agreement between governments.
2. IUCN runs thousands of field projects around the world to better manage natural environments.
3. CITES is legally binding on the States that have joined it, but this Conventional does not take the place of national laws.
questions.explain:
Statement 1 is incorrect: IUCN is not an organ of the United Nations. It is an international organization working in the field of nature conservation and sustainable use of natural resources.

Statement 2 is correct: IUCN runs thousands of field projects around the world to better manage natural environments.

Statement 3 is correct: CITES is legally binding on the parties, but it does not take the place of national laws. Rather, it provides a framework to be respected by each party, which has to adopt its own domestic legislation to ensure that CITES is implemented at the national level.

questions.q: If a wetland of international importance is brought under the 'Montreux Record', what does it imply?
options: Changes in ecological character have occurred, are occurring or are likely to occur in the wetland as a result of human interference.
The country in which the wetland is located should enact a law to prohibit any human activity within five kilometres from the edge of the wetland.
The survival of the wetland depends on the cultural practices and traditions of certain communities living in its vicinity and therefore the cultural diversity therein should not be destroyed.
It is given the status of 'World Heritage Site'.
questions.explain: The Montreux Record is a register of wetland sites on the List of Wetlands of International Importance where changes in ecological character have occurred, are occurring, or are likely to occur as a result of technological developments, pollution or other human interference. It is maintained as part of the Ramsar List.

questions.q: With reference to 'Global Environment Facility', which of the following statements is/are correct?
options: It serves as a financial mechanism for 'Convention on Biological Diversity' and 'United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change'.
It undertakes scientific research on environmental issues at global level.
It is an agency under OECD to facilitate the transfer of technology and funds to underdeveloped countries with specific aims to protect their environment.
questions.explain: The Global Environment Facility (GEF) was established on the eve of the 1992 Rio Earth Summit to help tackle our planet's most pressing environmental problems. It serves as a financial mechanism for 'Convention on Biological Diversity' and 'United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change'. It does not undertake scientific research on environmental issues at the global level, nor is it an agency under OECD.

questions.q: With reference to a conservation organisation called 'Wetlands International', which of the following statements is/are correct?\n1. It is an intergovernmental organisation formed by the countries which are signatories to the Ramsar Convention.\n2. It works at the field level to develop and mobilise knowledge and use the practical experience to advocate for better policies.
questions.explain: Statement 1 is not correct: Wetlands International is the only global not-for-profit organisation (not an intergovernmental organisation) dedicated to the conservation and restoration of wetlands. It is concerned about the loss and deterioration of wetlands such as lakes, marshes, and rivers. Wetlands International is dedicated to maintaining and restoring wetlands for their environmental values as well as for the services they provide to people.\n\nStatement 2 is correct: Wetland International-a network organisation working locally and globally. The organisation has a network of offices around the world; these often-independent entities share the same Strategy. They work at the field level to develop and mobilise knowledge and use this practical experience to advocate for better policies.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding 'Earth Hour'
1. It is an initiative of UNEP and UNESCO.
2. It is a movement in which the participants switch off the lights for one hour on a certain day every year.
3. It is a movement to raise awareness about climate change and the need to save the planet.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain:
Statement 1 is not correct: Earth Hour, organised by Worldwide Fund for Nature (WWF), is a global grassroots movement uniting people to take action on environmental issues and protect the planet.

Statement 2 is correct: Engaging a massive mainstream community, Earth Hour was famously started as a light-out event in Sydney, Australia in 2007. Since then, it has grown to engage millions of supporters in more than 185 countries and territories, inspiring individuals and organisations worldwide to take action for the environment and driving major legislative changes by harnessing the power of the crowd.

Statement 3 is correct: As the movement grows, the one-hour lights-out event continues to be the symbol of a broader commitment toward nature and our planet.

questions.q:
Consider the following international agreements:
1. The International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture.
2. The United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification.
3. The World Heritage Convention.
Which of the above has/have a bearing on biodiversity?
questions.explain:
Option 1 is correct: The International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture aims at recognizing the contribution of farmers to crop diversity, establishing a global system for plant genetic materials access, and ensuring benefits sharing.

Option 2 is correct: The United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD) addresses sustainable land management in drylands, aiming to restore degraded land, improve livelihoods, reduce drought impacts, and maintain biodiversity.

Option 3 is correct: The World Heritage Convention, adopted by UNESCO in 1972, is concerned with protecting World Cultural and Natural Heritage. It ensures global commitment to conserving biodiversity-rich places while respecting their cultural and local connections.

questions.q:
The Red Data Books published by the International Union for Conservation of Nature and Natural Resources (IUCN) contain lists of
1. Endemic plant and animal species present in the biodiversity hotspots.
2. Threatened plant and animal species.
3. Protected sites for conservation of nature and natural resources in various countries.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explain: Option (b) is correct: Red Books, a public document which is created for recording endangered threatened and rare species of plants, animals, fungi as well as some local subspecies that are present in a particular region is considered as a Red Data Book.\n\nIt gives complete information about research, and studies and, also for monitoring of the programs on rare and endangered species and their habitats. It is mainly created to identify and protect those species which are on the verge of extinction.

questions.q:
Three of the following criteria have contributed to the recognition of western Ghats, Sri Lanka and Indo-Burma regions as hotspots of biodiversity:
1. Species richness
2. Vegetation density
3. Endemism
4. Ethno-botanical importance
5. Threat perception
6. Adaptation of flora and fauna to warm and humid conditions
Which three of the above are correct criteria in this context?
questions.explain:
Option (c) is correct: The term Biodiversity hotspots Coined by Norman Myers can be defined as the regions which are known for their high species richness, threat perception and endemism. In 1989 and 1996, Conservation International (CI) adopted Myers' hotspots as its institutional blueprint and the organisation made the decision to undertake a reassessment of the hotspots concept.

India is known for its rich biodiversity and has 23.39% of its geographical area covered by forests and trees.

Biodiversity hotspot in India:
- Himalaya: Includes the entire Indian Himalayan region (and that falling in Pakistan, Tibet, Nepal, Bhutan, China and Myanmar).
- Indo-Burma: Includes entire North-eastern India, except Assam and Andaman group of Islands (and Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia and southern China).
- Sundalands: Includes Nicobar group of Islands (and Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Brunei, Philippines).
- Western Ghats and Sri Lanka: Includes the entire Western Ghats (and Sri Lanka).
